page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.4xlarge is an x86_64 virtual server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration supplies 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. It provides 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation with 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction set features include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage, and it includes no discrete GPU hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Standardized benchmark metrics place the instance in mid-tier performance bands. It delivers a stress-ng score of 1851.99 in single-core and 15444.6 in multi-core execution, a Geekbench single-core score of 1434.0, a multi-core score of 8709.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 19492.46. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 99.57 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 57.38 GB/sec.

With its 8 GB per vCPU ratio, the instance prioritizes memory capacity over compute density or high-speed local disk I/O. Benchmark testing demonstrates throughput capability of 15.56 million Redis SET operations per second and 16.54 GB/sec for static web serving. Qualitative cost efficiency is realized through its high memory density per compute core, making it effective for in-memory databases, key-value stores, enterprise application servers, and data preprocessing tasks that need abundant RAM without GPU or local NVMe overhead.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.4xlarge is an x86_64 instance built on an Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.5 GHz, provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 128.0 GB of RAM. Featuring an expanded 1:8 vCPU-to-memory configuration, the instance delivers 8.0 GB of memory per core alongside 33 MB of L3 cache, with AVX and AVX-512F instruction set support. The instance operates without bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and offering a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in mid-tier ranges, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 19492.46, multi-core Geekbench score of 8709.0, and Redis throughput of 15.56 million SET operations per second. This hardware profile provides resource efficiency for memory-heavy deployments, including in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise backend applications, and static web serving workloads requiring significant memory capacity.
